Tachograph for The Bus

Illustrated Guide to Operating the Device

Step by step, with real screenshots from the running app – even if you've never seen a tachograph before.

What even is a tachograph?

A tachograph is a device required by law in real trucks and buses. It automatically records how long a driver drives, works, takes breaks, or rests. This enforces the legal driving and rest time rules so nobody is driving while exhausted – in Switzerland and the EU, these are fixed limits.

This overlay recreates exactly such a device for The Bus: you insert a digital driver card, the device recognizes you as the driver, and records your times – just like in the real profession. There is no connection to real driver cards, GNSS, or a vehicle bus, and no data is sent to the game or the internet.

1. Device overview

After starting, the display briefly shows "echolino.com", then the main screen: time, speed, and today's distance. As long as no driver card is inserted, a small "no card" icon blinks on the left.

Main display.

A small icon appears on the bottom left whenever no driver card is inserted. The four buttons below the display – Back, Up, Down, OK – control the entire menu.

The driver card.

Every driver has their own card with a photo, name, and card number. It belongs in one of the two card slots (1 or 2) below the display.

2. Using the menu

Press OK to open the menu. Use the arrow buttons to scroll through the entries (e.g. printouts, vehicle data, time entries), and OK to select one. Back (↵) takes you one level up.

Inside the menu.

Here it shows "Printout · Driver 1" – one example menu entry. The arrow buttons take you further to "Driver 2", vehicle data, and more.

Leaving the menu.

Pressing Back all the way asks "Exit menu functions?". Confirm with OK on "Yes" to return to the main display.

3. Inserting a driver card

Before you start driving, your card belongs in the device – just like in a real bus. Here's how:

1Open the slot.

Hold the driver button (1 or 2, the ones with the person icons) for about two seconds. The slot opens and the card appears below the device, ready to insert.

2Click the card in.

Click the card to slide it into the open slot. The display briefly greets you with your name and the time.

3Confirm the time.

The device shows the date and time of the card's last use. Confirm the suggested values with OK – exactly like on a real device.

4Confirm the entry.

Finally, it asks "Confirm entry?". Press OK on "Yes" once more – done.

5Ready to drive!

The device shows "ready to drive". From now on it records automatically once you're on the road.

No numpad on your keyboard (e.g. a compact laptop layout)? All steps work exactly the same with the mouse.

4. Removing a driver card

At the end of your shift you take the card back out – the device asks for the country where you're ending the trip.

1Choose the country.

Hold the driver button for two seconds again. The device first asks for the country where the trip ends.

2Card removed.

The card now sits visibly below the device. You can click it again any time to re-insert it.

5. The other device model: VDO DTCO 1381

Besides the VDO DTCO 4.1, the settings also let you pick the older VDO DTCO 1381 model. Its control panel, menu wording and printouts differ noticeably from the DTCO 4.1 – the actual recording (driving, work and rest times) is identical on both models.

Switching the device model

In the settings (Ctrl+Alt+E) under "Device model", choose between VDO DTCO 4.1 and VDO DTCO 1381. The switch takes effect on the control panel immediately, without losing an inserted card or the recording made so far.

Operating the DTCO 1381

1At idle.

Redesigned control panel: a cross/D-pad (up/down/OK/back) with a separate extra button on the right in place of the printer slot, a row of 5 buttons right under the display, and the red plomb/seal centered between the two card slots – just like the real VDO DTCO 1381.

2Opening the menu.

Press OK on the D-pad to enter the menu (printout, entry, display). Navigate with the arrow keys around the ring, and go back with the key on the left side of the ring.

3Ejecting a card.

A short press on either eject button (⏏) in the 5-button row opens that card slot immediately – unlike the DTCO 4.1, a short press is enough here, no two-second hold needed.

4Inserting the card.

The driver card is ready and can be slid into the open slot. Clearly visible: the red plomb/seal and the D-pad with the extra button on the right.

5Card read.

The display briefly greets you with your name, local time and UTC time – done, recording is running.

You can switch the device model at any time without losing an inserted card or the recording made so far.

6. Tips & important keys

For players without a mouse (e.g. with a wheel setup) the whole device can also be controlled from the keyboard – deliberately only via Ctrl + Numpad, so nothing collides with The Bus's own keys.

ActionKey
Up / Down in menuCtrl+Num 8 / Ctrl+Num 2
OK / BackCtrl+Num 5 / Ctrl+Num 0
Switch activity driver 1 / 2Ctrl+Num 1 / Ctrl+Num 3
Eject driver card 1 / 2Ctrl+Num 4 / Ctrl+Num 6
Printer trayCtrl+Num 7
Tear off printoutCtrl+Num 9
Night mode (dimmed display)Ctrl+Alt+N
Settings (device model, export …)Ctrl+Alt+E

A connected controller (e.g. on a wheel setup) also controls the menu directly via its buttons.
